caption:
Same job. Same $90K salary. One of them pays $3,200 less income tax, legally.

Salary sacrifice sends part of your before-tax pay into super, where it's taxed at 15% instead of your marginal rate. In 2026–27, on $90K that's 30% plus the 2% Medicare levy. Sacrifice $10,000 and you save $3,200 in income tax, the fund takes $1,500, and you're about $1,700 ahead overall.

The catch: the money is locked in super until retirement, the 2026–27 concessional cap is $32,500 (your employer's 12% counts), lower incomes gain less, and over $250K Division 293 adds another 15%.

Save this for your next pay review.

General info only, not personal advice.

#salarysacrifice #superannuation #australiantax #moneytips #taxtips
figures_checked: 2026-27 resident rates: 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000; Medicare levy 2% (ATO Tax rates – Australian residents, checked 1 Nov 2026)
Concessional cap 2026-27 $32,500; carry-forward up to 5 years if total super balance < $500,000 (ATO Contributions caps / Concessional contributions cap, checked 1 Nov 2026)
Salary sacrifice taxed 15% in fund, employer must still pay full SG (ATO Salary sacrificing super, checked 1 Nov 2026)
Worked example: tax on $90K = $17,520 + $1,800 Medicare; on $80K = $14,520 + $1,600; difference $3,200; fund tax $1,500
